items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec asserts nameInput toHaveValue and header toContainText the new name (product-rename.spec.ts diff lines 105-107). Both would fail if the mutation never ran.
AC1 is asserted at diff line 101 (header after save). AC2 is asserted at lines 105-107 (name field and title after a reload).

No existing page object covers the product page, and no product-id lookup exists in e2e/lib or e2e/scenarios. ProductPage and findProductId are new and reuse gql/adminToken and the PRODUCTS and ORDERS_SCENARIO constants.
There are no fixed waits. rename() waits on a web-first toBeDisabled assertion, and goto waits on nameInput.
It uses the fixture test from ../../fixtures/test.ts with the orders scenario, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
Locators use data-test-ids that exist in src (page-header, product-general-settings, button-bar-confirm) plus a role locator for the Name textbox scoped to the general settings card.
The product comes from the orders scenario. The spec only reads its id through a lookup and changes nothing during Arrange.
There are no hard-coded ids. The product is looked up by its scenario name (PRODUCTS.hoodie.name), not by populatedb data.
It uses the default admin stored session, which suits a general staff rename story. There is no UI login and no credentials.
typecheck.txt reports 'exit 0: no errors'. The spec is at e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts.
All locators and the rename action live on ProductPage. The spec only calls page.reload() inline.
Members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and the class uses constructor(readonly page: Page) {} (productPage.ts diff lines 12-20).
It has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (diff lines 91, 98).
One test tells the story, with a test.step for saving and one for the reload check.
The title 'Staff renames a product and the new name is saved #e2e' describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
The header comment (diff lines 82-85) explains what is covered and why a reload is used.
All assertions are web-first (toContainText, toHaveValue, toBeDisabled).
The scenario name and the original product name come from ORDERS_SCENARIO and PRODUCTS. The new name is the ticket's own literal, which no scenario constant holds.
There is no cleanup code and no unique names.
There are no per-test timeouts or retries, no networkidle, and no waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension. The spec takes test/expect only from the fixture. The page object imports expect from @playwright/test, as draftOrderPage.ts and homePage.ts already do.
The gql call in findProductId has a typed response, and there are no any types or casts.
The comments explain reasons (why Save turning disabled means the form has settled, why the search result is matched exactly, why a reload is used) rather than narrating.

structured_output.summary: I judged submission e78cc5bf as meeting all 23 checklist items. The spec reloads the page and checks that both the name field and the page title show "E2E Zip Hoodie", so the test would fail if the rename never saved. It starts from the existing orders test data, finds the product by its known name, and adds a small ProductPage page object written like the existing ones. Type checking passes.
